policy_title: Advocate for Immediate Bilateral Ceasefire in Israel-Gaza
stated: Advocate for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in the Israel-Gaza conflict to resolve the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, get the hostages out, and provide the space to reach a two-state solution based on 1967 borders with security and dignity for Israelis and Palestinians.

source.quote: Advocate for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in the Israel-Gaza conflict to resolve the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, get the hostages out, and provide the space to reach a two-state solution based on 1967 borders with security and dignity for Israelis and Palestinians.

bearing_set.reason: UK foreign policy advocacy on a live armed conflict directly bears on national security and defence posture — the stated position shapes diplomatic alliances, domestic radicalisation risk, and the UK's international security commitments, all explicit O5 indicators.

The Israel-Gaza conflict has had documented effects on UK inter-community relations (antisemitic and anti-Muslim hate crimes both rose sharply post-October 2023); how UK government positions itself on the conflict materially affects social trust and inter-group tensions across Jewish, Muslim and wider communities domestically.

membership_note: This is primarily a foreign-policy advocacy position; its direct domestic bearing is on national security posture (O5) and community cohesion (O15), where concrete mechanisms exist. Effects on O9 (international Palestinian/Israeli rights) are outside the fundamentals' domestic scope; effects on O2/O11/O12/O13 are too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
